findings.evidence: Line 220 `private lemma mem_range_lineMap_iff`; line 235 hypothesis `hS : S ⊆ Set.range (AffineMap.lineMap (k := ℝ) p q)`; grep for `range_lineMap`/`mem_range.*lineMap` in ./mathlib returns no matches.
findings.fix: Drop `private` from `mem_range_lineMap_iff` (making it public) so the general theorem's hypothesis can be discharged without unfolding; the two in-file special cases already rely on it, confirming it is the intended entry point.
findings.issue: `mem_range_lineMap_iff` is `private`, yet it is the only characterization of the `S ⊆ Set.range (AffineMap.lineMap (k := ℝ) p q)` hypothesis of the exposed general theorem `differentiableOn_of_continuousOn_of_differentiableOn_diff_of_subset_range_lineMap`. Mathlib provides no such range characterization, so a consumer applying the general theorem to an arbitrary line/segment (the roadmap's 'arc of a line') must unfold `AffineMap.lineMap` by hand — an incomplete characteristic API for the exported result.

summary: The five public removability theorems form a minimal, body-hidden surface and the base case is consumed cleanly by the reflection principle. But the general line theorem's hypothesis `S ⊆ range (lineMap p q)` has no public characterization: its only bridge, `mem_range_lineMap_iff`, is private, so external consumers cannot build the hypothesis without unfolding `AffineMap.lineMap`.
